title: Capacity Orchestration Experiments & Q2 Playbook — Dedicated Pools + Predictive Autoscale
creator: Anika Patel
description: Goal: Produce a runnable Q2 playbook that proves two predictive autoscale strategies for dedicated GPU pools (time-series demand predictor + fast-warm reservoir) and a set of measurable rollout criteria. Scope includes experiment design, metric instrumentation, dashboarding, two canary rollouts, and a decision gate for GA readiness. This ticket consolidates PM-level milestones, success metrics, and cross-functional asks for Eng, SRE, Console, and Billing.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc with experiment matrix and traffic slices approved by Eng and SRE
Two independent autoscale strategies implemented in staging and smoke-tested under synthetic traffic
Dashboards show warm-pool utilization, prewarm latency, cost delta per token, and failure/retry rates
Canary rollout plan with rollback triggers and runbook validated in one customer-simulated scenario
Decision: one strategy recommended for Q3 soft-launch or clear reasons to iterate further
milestones: 2025-02-07: Experiment design and success metrics finalized
2025-02-21: Instrumentation landed and dashboard prototype published
2025-03-28: PM decision gate and playbook published
risks: Predictive model cold-starts lead to spike in prewarm cost without latency gains
KV cache warming behavior in long-tail workloads may invalidate synthetic test results
Insufficient visibility into per-route cost makes tradeoffs hard to quantify
Customer-facing degradation if rollback automation is incomplete
decisions: Use two independent strategies in parallel rather than iterative A/B to collect orthogonal signals
Scope excludes changes to tenancy or pricing contract language for this quarter — billing implications will be a follow-up
All canary runs must include one real customer traffic mirror where the customer has opted in
